facts.text: SpotMicroEnv-v0 is registered with entry point spotmicro.spot_gym_env:spotGymEnv and max_episode_steps 1000
spotGymEnv simulates the locomotion of a quadruped robot; its docstring says the action space is the desired motor angle for each motor
NUM_MOTORS is 12
The action bound _action_bound is 1
The action space is spaces.Box(-action_high, action_high) with action_high made of _action_bound for action_dim = NUM_MOTORS
The observation bounds come from Spot.GetObservationUpperBound() plus OBSERVATION_EPS and GetObservationLowerBound() minus OBSERVATION_EPS
The observation upper bound is 2*pi for roll and pitch, infinity for the three angular rates and three linear accelerations, 2.0 for the four leg phases and 1.0 for the four contacts
The observation lower bound is minus the upper bound
GetObservation appends roll, pitch, the angular twist xyz, the linear acceleration xyz, the leg phases and, when contacts are enabled, the four foot contacts
The contacts constructor option defaults to True
is_fallen returns true when the dot product of the world up direction and the base's local up direction is below 0.55
_termination returns is_fallen() or whether the base distance exceeds _distance_limit
distance_limit defaults to float('inf')
The simulation time step is 0.01 s and the control period is _time_step * _action_repeat
action_repeat defaults to 1, and pd_control_enabled and accurate_motor_model_enabled default to False
seed calls gym.utils.seeding.np_random and returns [seed]
step returns a numpy observation, the reward, done and an empty info dictionary
env_randomizer defaults to a SpotEnvRandomizer instance
SpotEnvRandomizer seeds numpy's global generator with 0 in its constructor
The constructor creates a pybullet_utils BulletClient, so the environment runs on PyBullet
The environment metadata declares the human and rgb_array render modes and 50 video frames per second

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 seeds the fake and its placeholder initial tilt and gait phase; upstream seeds gym.utils.seeding.np_random and the default SpotEnvRandomizer then draws physical properties from numpy's global generator, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two implementations

gaps: the fake is a pure Python kinematic stand-in with placeholder tilt, gait-phase, acceleration and reward values; it does not run PyBullet and models no rigid bodies, contacts, motor model or actuator fidelity, so trajectories differ from the clone

the fake models no sensor noise, control or observation latency, observation history, height field or environment randomizer; upstream SpotEnvRandomizer randomizes mass, inertia, friction, battery voltage and motor damping at every reset

the fake reset returns (observation, info) and its step returns a five-tuple with the registered 1000-step limit applied by the fake; upstream reset returns the observation only and step returns a four-tuple, and gym.make adds the TimeLimit wrapper
the fake seeds Python's random.Random; upstream seeds gym.utils.seeding.np_random and the randomizer uses numpy's global generator, so the same seed gives different trajectories
no rendering, camera adjustment or GUI pacing is modelled; realtime_factor 0 and ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulated spot world stops advancing: after an e-stop every step and reset is refused and the last observation stays readable until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; there is no hardware to stop
